title: Smooth sum invariance bound
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ be real-valued random variables on (possibly different) probability spaces, with each family independent. Assume every variable has finite third absolute moment, and for each $i$ the means and second moments of $X_i$ and $Y_i$ agree. If $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is three times continuously differentiable and $C\ge0$ satisfies $|\psi'''(t)|\le C$ for every real $t$, then the absolute difference between the expectations of $\psi(\sum_i X_i)$ and $\psi(\sum_i Y_i)$ is at most $\frac C6\sum_i\bigl(\mathbb E|X_i|^3+\mathbb E|Y_i|^3\bigr)$.
hypotheses_covered: Both underlying spaces carry probability measures
Each $X_i$ has finite third absolute moment
Each $Y_i$ has finite third absolute moment
Corresponding variables have equal second moments
